I've been affected by this since the sunset date. Two specific pain points:

1. **Switching sessions requires navigating to the home page first** - in the old layout, the project sidebar with sessions was always visible, so switching was one click. Now it takes an extra step every time.
2. **Tab titles don't show project name or path** - I work across multiple projects and can't distinguish which project a tab belongs to without hovering. Issue #37273 captures this.

The asar patching workaround breaks on every update. A simple env var like OPENCODE_USE_LEGACY_LAYOUT=1 would solve this immediately. +1
I have this too (I was writing up a report and the duplicate detector sent me here).

- **OpenCode version:** 1.18.31 (also tested on this exact version as the reporter)

Endorsing the ask from those threads: strip/drop stale `encrypted_content` on retry (keep summary) instead of blind retry, so one bad turn doesn't brick the whole session.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #42263: Same root cause — base64-encoded binary (PDFs in that case) persisted verbatim into SQLite tool-result records and duplicated across turns, causing storage bloat and memory issues. The suggested fixes overlap significantly with yours.
- #36343: Overlapping symptom — image base64 is stored twice in the tool-success event (structured output + model content), which is the same duplication you observe in the v2 `session_message` record.

Update: resolved. Turns out it was our configuration, not opencode.

Our baseURL was missing the /v1 segment, and a later rollback had also switched us to the OpenAI-compatible protocol (where no cache marks are sent). After switching back to @ai-sdk/anthropic with https://api.ofox.ai/anthropic/v1, the proxy reports 100% cache hit rate
(creation 762k / read 381k tokens on a 3-request test).

Thanks to everyone who helped narrow this down — the passthrough-capture evidence and OfoxAI's engineering reply were decisive. Leaving the issue to maintainers for the remaining `anthropic/`-prefixed model id thread. 🐙

I re-checked `v2` this round and found that the behaviour #36761 asks for is already there, so I'm withdrawing this PR instead of asking for review time on a duplicate.

`packages/core/src/tool/plugin/subagent.ts` appends the requested catalog to the model-facing tool description from a session context hook:

```ts
const hook = (event: SessionHooks["context"]) =>
  Effect.gen(function* () {
    const tool = event.tools[name]
    if (!tool) return
    const selected = yield* agents.resolve(event.agent)
    if (!selected) return
    const available = (yield* agents.list())
      .filter(
        (agent) =>
          agent.mode !== "primary" &&
          !agent.hidden &&
          Permission.evaluate(name, agent.id, selected.permissions).effect !== "deny",
      )
      .toSorted((a, b) => a.id.localeCompare(b.id))
    if (available.length === 0) return
    tool.description = [
      tool.description,
      "",
      "Available subagents:",
      ...available.map(
        (agent) =>
          `- ${agent.id}: ${agent.description ?? "This subagent should only be called when explicitly requested."}`,
      ),
    ].join("\n")
  })
yield* ctx.session.hook("context", hook)
yield* ctx.session.hook("compaction", hook)
yield* ctx.session.hook("generate", hook)
```

That is exactly what the issue asked for — "a compact permission-filtered catalog in the tool description": Location-specific via `agents.list()`, mode-filtered (`mode !== "primary" && !hidden`), permission-filtered for the caller, exact IDs, sorted. #48749 additionally runs the same hook for compaction and generate requests.

This PR attacked the same problem on a different surface: it injected the IDs into the `agent` input field's description (`makeInput(agentDescription)`) rather than the tool description. That would not make the IDs any more discoverable, and the tool description is the surface the issue requested, so the change adds nothing.

It was also already redundant when I opened it. The context hook at `d94d520f4` (2026-08-15) and `7188d42b9` (2026-08-18) carried the same listing, i.e. before this PR was created on 2026-08-18. That is my error: I verified the static `agent` input description and did not check what the session hooks append to `tool.description` before claiming #36761. Apologies for the noise on that issue.

Withdrawing; no rebase planned, and the branch is conflicted against `v2` anyway (`DIRTY`). This can be closed. If you would rather have the IDs surfaced in the input field as well, tell me and I will rebase instead.

Subject: opencode desktop app constantly breaks with "Failed to fetch" - needs a fix

Hi,

I'm reporting a serious bug in the opencode desktop app (v1.18.31, Windows 11).

Problem: After about 10-15 minutes of inactivity, the app stops working completely. The next time I try to send a message or use the app, it fails with:

TypeError: Failed to fetch
    at fetch (oc://renderer/assets/main-mfFBJ4oT.js:161276:45)
    at request (oc://renderer/assets/main-mfFBJ4oT.js:52365:24)
    at async createResource.initialValue (oc://renderer/assets/index-CIoSNsin.js:326:48)
The only way to fix it is to close and restart the app. This keeps happening all day, every day.

What I already checked and ruled out:

Stable Ethernet connection (1 Gbps), no network drops
No laptop sleep/standby during the failure
The local server is healthy (responds in 1-2 ms), and it never restarts during a session
Wi-Fi power saving disabled, AC sleep set to never
What's happening (my diagnosis): The app's renderer (WebView2/Chromium) drops its idle keep-alive connection to the local server after ~10-15 minutes, and the app never retries or reconnects. So every request after that point fails.

Why it matters: This makes the desktop app unusable for longer work sessions. The terminal version (opencode in a terminal) does not have this problem at all — it reconnects fine.

Request: Please add auto-retry/reconnect logic to the renderer's fetch layer so the app reconnects without needing a manual restart.

Happy to share logs if needed.

Thanks!

Additional diagnostic evidence for the config-driven default mentioned in this issue (OpenCode Desktop 1.18.31, macOS).

The global JSONC config contains:
```json
{
  "permission": "allow",
  "default_agent": "build"
}
```
On an existing installation, a new session starts in Build, but Auto-accept is not shown as enabled. After reloading Desktop, the actual config response was inspected in its DevTools Network panel: `default_agent` is `"build"`, while `permission` is an **object** containing `"*": "allow"`. This installation also has an existing legacy tool rule that becomes another entry in that object. No full config, credentials, local paths, or screenshots are attached.

There appears to be a representation mismatch in the v1.18.31 config-driven initialization path:

1. [ConfigPermissionV1 normalization](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.18.31/packages/core/src/v1/config/permission.ts) converts a string action into an object:
```ts
const normalizeInput = (input: Schema.Schema.Type<typeof InputSchema>): Schema.Schema.Type<typeof InputObject> =>
  typeof input === "string" ? { "*": input } : input
```
2. [Desktop permission state](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.18.31/packages/app/src/context/permission.tsx), in `enableConfiguredDirectory(directory)`, checks:
```ts
if (input.sdk.protocolKind() !== "v1") return
// ...
if (childStore.config.permission !== "allow") return
```
`isPermissionAllowAll(directory)` in the same file also uses strict string equality.

An object response cannot pass that string check. This looks like a concrete issue with the intended bridge from the documented global `permission: "allow"` setting to the Desktop default, rather than a missing global config setting.

Scope/limitations: the config response and visible symptom were verified, but this is not yet a clean-profile reproduction, the active protocol branch was not instrumented, and existing directory/session overrides were not ruled out. We have NOT demonstrated that server-side tool permissions fail or that tools actually prompt with this config. The finding concerns automatic initialization of the client-side Auto-accept state. **Correction — OpenCode version matters:**

My earlier comment recommended `github:arfoux/rs-guard`, but that plugin is **OpenCode V2 only** (`@opencode/plugin` v2 API: `context`/`compaction`/`generate` + `retry` hooks for stateless replay and retry-without-reasoning). It will not load on OpenCode V1.

- **OpenCode V2** — full self-heal (`github:arfoux/rs-guard`):
  ```sh
  opencode plugin add github:arfoux/rs-guard
  ```
  Forces stateless full replay on every request (no `previous_response_id`, `store: false`, no `include: reasoning.encrypted_content`), strips server-issued ids (`rs_*`, `msg_*`) from metadata, keeps at most 1 newest encrypted blob. On a matching error it retries once with no reasoning at all.
- **OpenCode V1** — best-effort (`github:arfoux/rs-guard-v1`):
  ```sh
  opencode plugin add github:arfoux/rs-guard-v1
  ```
  V1 (`@opencode-ai/plugin`) has no request/retry hooks, so it works with what V1 offers: `chat.params` strips `include: reasoning.encrypted_content` / continuation ids and forces `store: false`; `experimental.chat.messages.transform` strips stale ids/blobs; `experimental.session.compacting` keeps reasoning state out of summaries; `session.error` shows a guidance toast (retry, or fresh session if it persists).

**Tested on:** `muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free` via Gateway Console — fails on message 2–3 without the plugin, works consistently with the V2 plugin. (For the report by @egkike on opencode 1.18.31 / V1: use `rs-guard-v1`; it reduces the failure surface but cannot auto-retry — if the error still appears, just retry, or start a fresh session.)

**Caveat:** Both are client-side mitigations, not a server fix. The root cause is upstream replaying stale encrypted/reasoning state that the Console free tier rejects. Same family as #28678 / #29000 but for Console/Gateway models.

I am seeing caller-provided casing reach OpenCode `read`, `glob`, and Git snapshot operations inside a Linux devcontainer whose workspace is bind-mounted from case-insensitive macOS through Docker Desktop virtiofs.

This PR appears not to cover that case because:

- OpenCode reports `process.platform === "linux"` inside the container.
- Canonicalization is currently applied to session locations, not file-tool or snapshot paths.
- Resolving the already wrong-case path may itself trigger the known Docker Desktop virtiofs casing issue: https://github.com/docker/desktop-feedback/issues/251

The resulting OpenCode snapshot error is:

```text
fatal: will not add file alias 'app/app.vue' ('app/App.vue' already exists in index)
```

The mount can subsequently expose both casing variants, causing directory scanners such as TypeScript to report TS1149.

A broader mitigation may need to canonicalize tracked file paths from the complete Git index before any filesystem lookup, and apply that consistently to `read`, `glob`, edit, and snapshot operations. For Linux containers, checking only `process.platform === "darwin"` will not detect that the backing filesystem is case-insensitive macOS/virtiofs.

**A second gap that I don't think has been mentioned yet:** the existing prune pass can't help even when it does run, because it budgets by *text* only:

- `SessionCompaction.prune` walks old completed tool parts and sums `Token.estimate(part.state.output)` against `PRUNE_PROTECT = 40_000` (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/3104c1428e/packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts#L286-L318, estimate at L299).
- For an image `read`, `state.output` is the 23-char string `Image read successfully`; the attachment (base64 bytes, image count) is not part of the estimate. So 52 screenshots ≈ 0 tokens, the budget is never exceeded and nothing gets `time.compacted`.

Suggestion, complementary to #47493's per-request cap: make prune count attachments too (a fixed token weight per image attachment, and/or an attachment-count budget), so old screenshots get `time.compacted` like any other large tool output. Once the flag is set, `toModelMessages` already does the right thing: `[Old tool result content cleared]` + attachments dropped (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/3104c1428e/packages/opencode/src/session/message-v2.ts#L293-L296).

**Recovery that works today for a bricked session** (same mechanism prune uses, fully reversible — just delete the key):

```python
import sqlite3, json, time
db = sqlite3.connect('~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db'.replace('~', __import__('os').path.expanduser('~')))
sid = 'ses_...'; keep_after_ms = 0  # e.g. time_created of the first part you still want as an image
rows = db.execute("""select id, data from part where session_id=? and json_extract(data,'$.type')='tool'
  and json_extract(data,'$.state.status')='completed'
  and json_array_length(json_extract(data,'$.state.attachments'))>0
  and json_extract(data,'$.state.time.compacted') is null and time_created < ?""", (sid, keep_after_ms)).fetchall()
now = int(time.time()*1000)
for pid, data in rows:
    d = json.loads(data); d['state']['time']['compacted'] = now
    db.execute("update part set data=?, time_updated=? where id=?", (json.dumps(d, ensure_ascii=False), now, pid))
db.commit()
```

Back up `opencode.db` first. Verified on 1.18.30: 35 old image parts flagged → 17 images sent → session usable again, no restart needed (history is re-read from the DB on each turn). Only `state.time.compacted` is touched — don't put anything non-object into the part's top-level `metadata`, that field is forwarded as `providerOptions` and will fail the AI SDK `ModelMessage[]` schema.

Still reproduces on **1.18.31** (this was filed against 1.18.7). Source reading below in case it saves someone the trip.

## Where it breaks

`packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx`:

```ts
const children = createMemo(() => {
  const parentID = session()?.parentID ?? session()?.id
  return sync.data.session
    .filter((x) => x.parentID === parentID || x.id === parentID)
    .toSorted((a, b) => (a.id < b.id ? -1 : a.id > b.id ? 1 : 0))
})
const permissions = createMemo(() => {
  if (session()?.parentID) return []
  return children().flatMap((x) => sync.data.permission[x.id] ?? [])
})
```

Two defects that compound:

1. `children()` collects **direct children only** — one level, not a recursive descendant walk. Viewed from the root it holds level-1 sessions; a level-2 session id is never in that list, so its entry in `sync.data.permission[...]` is never read.
2. `permissions()` returns `[]` whenever `session()?.parentID` is truthy, i.e. from **any** non-root view — so navigating into the subagent view does not help either.

Net effect: a permission raised at depth 2 is unreachable from every view. Depth 1 works only because a level-1 session happens to be a direct child of the root.

The request itself is fine. `packages/tui/src/context/sync.tsx` stores it correctly under its own session id (`setStore("permission", request.sessionID, [request])`), and the event is broadcast per directory/workspace with no session filter. It is purely the render layer that drops it.

Worth noting that `PermissionV1.Request` (`packages/schema/src/v1/permission.ts`) carries only `sessionID` — no `parentID` or `rootID` — so the view has nothing to walk up with even if it wanted to.

## It hangs rather than failing

`packages/opencode/src/permission/index.ts` blocks on `Deferred.await(deferred)` with no timeout anywhere in that file. The only thing that ever resolves it is the instance-state finalizer on teardown. So the call does not fail, it hangs until the session is killed — which is why `blocked (1)` in the status bar is the only visible symptom.

## Please don't fix only `permissions()`

Three lines below, `questions()` has the identical short-circuit and the same one-level `children()`:

```ts
const questions = createMemo(() => {
  if (session()?.parentID) return []
  return children().flatMap((x) => sync.data.question[x.id] ?? [])
})
```

#30635 was closed having fixed a single level of nesting, which is why this issue, #43996 and #44747 are all still open. A complete fix needs three things together: make `children()` walk descendants recursively, drop the non-root bail-out, and cover `questions()` in the same patch. I filed the `questions()` half as #49342 so it stays trackable — it is the same root cause, not a separate bug.

## Our repro

Three levels, `external_directory` left at the default `ask`: an orchestrator agent delegates to a general-purpose subagent, which delegates to a read-only explorer subagent. The explorer globs a directory outside the worktree. The status bar shows `blocked (1)`, no dialog renders in any view, and the turn never ends. Our configuration ships `subagent_depth: 10`, so depth-2 chains are routine rather than exotic — which is probably why we hit this on day one of using them.

As a workaround we have had to set `external_directory` to `allow` with an explicit `deny` floor over sensitive directories, because the alternative is pre-granting every external path a user might ever touch. We would much rather go back to `ask`.

One detail for whoever writes the fix: `external_directory` asks about `path.join(path.dirname(target), "*")` (`packages/opencode/src/tool/external-directory.ts`), never the file path — so a `deny` floor can only ever be directory-granular. That is fine, but it surprised us, and it may be worth a line in the permission docs.
